messages.content: What are the different properties of Hydrogen?

message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic** | Symbol | H |
| | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Atomic radius | ~53 pm (covalent) |
| | Van der Waals radius | ~120 pm |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | First ionization energy | 13.598 eV |
| | Electron affinity | 0.754 eV |
| | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride) |
| | Nuclear spin | ½ (¹H), 0 (²H), ½ (³H) |
| | Isotopes | ¹H (protium), ²H (deuterium), ³H (tritium) |
| | Half‑life of ³H | 12.32 yr |
| **Physical** | State at STP | Gas |
| | Color | Colorless |
| | Odor | Odorless |
| | Taste | Tasteless |
| | Density (STP) | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume (STP) | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C |
| | Specific heat (gas) | 14.304 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Thermal conductivity | 0.180 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Diffusivity | Very high (fastest among gases) |
| **Chemical** | Bond type | Diatomic (H₂) |
| | Bond dissociation energy | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Reactivity | Highly reactive; forms hydrides, acids, organics |
| | Combustion reaction | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (exothermic) |
| | Acid–base behavior | Acts as a weak acid (HF) or base (NaH) depending on context |
| | Halogen‑like behavior | Shares some properties with halogens (e.g., electronegativity, reactivity) |
| **Spectroscopic** | Lyman series (UV) | 121.6 nm (Hα) |
| | Balmer series (visible) | 656.3 nm (Hα), 486.1 nm (Hβ) |
| | Infrared absorption | 2.5 µm (H₂ vibrational) |
| | Raman shift | 4155 cm⁻¹ (H₂) |
| **Nuclear** | Stability | ¹H stable, ²H stable, ³H radioactive |
| | Nuclear reactions | Fusion (p + p → d + e⁺ + νₑ), fission (in bombs) |
| | Energy release | ~0.7 % mass defect → ~0.8 MeV per reaction |
| **Applications** | Fuel | Hydrogen fuel cells, rocket propellant |
| | Industry | Production of ammonia (Haber process), methanol, etc. |
| | Medicine | MRI contrast agents (tritium labeling) |
| | Research | Spectroscopy, quantum chemistry, astrophysics |
| | Energy | Potential clean energy carrier (hydrogen economy) |

---

### Quick Highlights

- **Non‑metal, diatomic gas** that is the lightest element.
- **Electronegativity 2.20** places it between alkali metals and halogens.
- **First ionization energy 13.6 eV** – the highest among all elements.
- **Boiling point –252.9 °C**; melts at –259.2 °C.
- **Density 0.0899 g L⁻¹** – far lighter than air.
- **Isotopes**: ¹H (stable), ²H (stable, used in heavy water), ³H (radioactive, half‑life 12.3 yr).
- **Spectral lines**: Lyman‑α at 121.6 nm, Balmer‑α at 656.3 nm.
- **Uses**: from everyday fuels to advanced research and medicine.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property!
